comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C1-C31). Both evaluations recognize these as well-established facts from prior literature that are appropriately supported by citations and serve as context for the current work.

Perfect agreement on CTD crosslinking to Tim23 and Tim17 (C32, C58-C62). Both evaluations recognize this as one of the most important observations, with strong support from in vivo crosslinking experiments. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong agreement on NTD-Tim23 interaction via loop 1 (C33, C66-C67). Both evaluations recognize this as a key finding supported by the truncated Tim23 construct. OpenEval also includes additional claims (C63-C65) about Tim23 structure that peer reviewers accepted separately (R13).

Significant disagreement on NTD intrinsic disorder (C34, C83-C86). OpenEval finds the convergence of computational predictions, HSQC NMR, and CD spectroscopy provides strong support. Peer reviewers express major concerns that recombinant protein in E. coli may not reflect native state and request the interpretation be softened or substantiated with additional evidence.

Partial disagreement on NTD-presequence binding (C74-C81). OpenEval finds the systematic in vitro crosslinking experiments provide strong support for the interaction and binding site mapping. Peer reviewers acknowledge the finding as important but request additional experiments to test whether presequence binding causes conformational changes in the NTD.

Significant disagreement on D345 mutant characterization (C38-C49). OpenEval finds multiple complementary approaches strongly support functional importance. Peer reviewers express concern that defects might reflect general translocon dysfunction rather than specific motor coupling defects, requesting additional in vitro import experiments with motor-dependent and -independent preproteins.

Similar disagreement on nearby residue mutants (C50-C57). OpenEval finds convergence of multiple experimental approaches strengthens conclusions. Peer reviewers request more thorough characterization to distinguish motor coupling defects from general channel dysfunction, and question the statement about Tim23 interaction being more important than Tim17.

Disagreement on suppressor analysis (C68-C73). OpenEval finds the convergence of genetic and biochemical data strongly supports functional communication between NTD and CTD. Peer reviewers find it interesting but request substantial additional characterization including translocase integrity, import experiments, and consideration of whether suppression works through altered presequence interaction.

Disagreement on interpretive model (C36-C37, C88-C89). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by collective experimental data and provides a coherent framework. Peer reviewers implicitly question the model by requesting experiments on translocase dynamics, indicating they view it as insufficiently supported without data on how interactions change during substrate binding and mtHsp70 reaction cycle.

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic model (C103-C109). Both evaluations recognize this detailed mechanistic model as speculative. OpenEval notes most specific steps lack direct experimental validation. Peer reviewers request experiments on translocase dynamics to support the model.

Agreement on uncertainty of comparative claims (C90-C91). OpenEval notes C90 lacks systematic quantitative comparison and C91 is explicitly speculative. Peer reviewers specifically question the data source for the statement about Tim23 being more important than Tim17.

Agreement on NTD regulatory center (C97-C100). Both evaluations support the conclusion that this region serves as a regulatory center based on convergence of multiple interaction sites. Peer reviewers requested additional experiments on conformational changes but did not question the identification of functional importance.

Perfect agreement on IDP principles (C101-C102). Both evaluations recognize these as well-established general principles about intrinsically disordered proteins, appropriately supported by citations to relevant reviews.
Perfect agreement on prior literature (C110). Both evaluations recognize this as appropriately cited prior work that was not questioned.

Agreement on Tim17 loop 3 and alternative models (C92-C96). OpenEval finds C92-C93 supported by citations. Peer reviewers accepted these along with the alternative models (C94-C96) presented as possibilities rather than definitive conclusions.

Agreement on uncertainty of alternative models (C94-C96). OpenEval notes both models are plausible but lack direct experimental evidence to distinguish between them. Peer reviewers did not critique these alternative possibilities.

Agreement on D345 structural context (C39-C40). Both evaluations accept the sequence conservation analysis and structural observations as supporting context for functional studies. These were not questioned by peer reviewers.
Agreement on Tim23 structural facts (C63-C65). Both evaluations recognize these as supported by citations and providing necessary context for crosslinking experiments.
Agreement on prior NTD observations (C74, C82). Both evaluations recognize these as appropriately cited prior observations from literature that provide context for current experiments.

Agreement on prior NTD disorder prediction (C82). Both evaluations accept this prior observation from literature as context, though they disagree on the strength of current experimental evidence for disorder (see R8 vs R3 comparison).
